newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers vote to merge.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers vote to merge.

text.p: The United Steelworkers of America said Tuesday that the 40,000-member Aluminum, Brick & Glass Workers International Union voted to merge with the steelworkers union.

The vote by more than 400 ABGW delegates representing 230 unions came in a secret ballot at a special convention on Monday. The vote was 374 to 86, or 81 percent in favour of the merger, well over the two-thirds needed for ratification, the steelworkers union said.

The ABG and the steelworkers union have worked together for many years, and "our two unions fit together naturally," said George Becker, president of the steelworkers union, which will now have about 740,000 members.
During the debate on the merger, many delegates emphasised the need for greater strength to deal with growing attacks on unions by companies and many governments.
The delegates also noted that by merging with the steelworkers, they will take part in the merger of the Auto Workers and Machinists unions with the steelworkers union, scheduled for the year 2000.
A proposed merger had been approved by the executive committees of the ABG and steelworkers last August and submitted to ABG locals for review before the convention.

Under the agreement, the merger will become effective Jan. 20, 1997. After the merger, all ABG local unions will constitute the Aluminum, Brick and Glass Division of the steelworkers union based in St. Louis, where the ABG is now based.
The division will have its own elected officers and a seat on the steelworkers' executive board.
